claims.text: TaNbHfZrTi is a refractory high-entropy alloy suitable for the proposed thin-film study.
Combining in situ ultrafast pump-probe spectroscopy with a VDOS model will reliably identify refractory HEA thin films having low phonon thermal conductivity.
Multi-element mass disorder and strain produce distinctive modifications of optical phonon modes in refractory HEA thin films.
Multi-element mass disorder and strain reduce phonon lifetimes in the proposed films.
Reduced phonon lifetimes decrease phonon mean free paths.
The resulting decrease in phonon mean free path lowers phonon thermal conductivity.
Ultrafast pump-probe spectroscopy can capture the disorder- and strain-induced vibrational changes relevant to low thermal conductivity.
A mass-disorder-adjusted VDOS model can accurately represent the measured phonon lifetimes and spectral features.
The combined approach will predict phonon thermal conductivity to within ±10% of measured values.
Traditional steady-state or static models typically deviate by ±20–30% when predicting phonon thermal conductivity.
A distinct spectral signature will correlate with reduced phonon lifetimes.
Temperature-dependent transport measurements over 300–800 K are experimentally feasible.
Laser-flash analysis can provide an independent thermal-conductivity benchmark for the proposed thin-film TaNbHfZrTi samples.
HEA transport-property predictions must be compared with experimental data to assess their validity.
The approach is applicable only to thin-film refractory HEAs in the 300–800 K range.
Sample-density variations and uncalibrated spectral noise can limit interpretation of the measurements.
Prediction accuracy depends on calibration and on isolating intrinsic phonon-lifetime effects from extraneous signals.
